entry:gpai-cop:cov.note: All nine coverage elements are supported, timing included (trigger points in the Framework, full assessment before placing on the market). Measure 4.1 tiers are capability-based, measurable and set by signatories; the 10^25 FLOP presumption is the Act's. Commitment 6 (legal text Art. 55(1)) and Appendices 4.2–4.5 cover unreleased parameters, interfaces, physical access, insider threats, external security reviews and red-teaming. Measure 5.1 lists filtering, refusals and staged access; marking falls under the separate Art. 50 code. Model Report updates go to the AI Office at least every six months; non-signatories must justify alternative compliance.

entry:eu-aia:cov:acct.note: Incident reporting (Art. 55(1)(c)), access (Art. 92(3)), recall (Art. 93(1)(c)) and €15M/3% (Art. 101) verified, but the Digital Omnibus moved supervision of AI systems built on a provider's own GPAI model, and their high-risk incident reports, to the AI Office (new Art. 75(1), (1a)).

entry:eu-aia:cov:update.note: Codes reviewable (Art. 56(8)); delegated acts amend the thresholds (Art. 51(3)) and Annex III (Art. 7(1)); other changes need legislation (as the 2026 Omnibus itself shows).

gap:elicit.note: Factual core verified: the AI Act requires adversarial testing (Art. 55(1)(a)) but not elicitation by name; the GPAI Code explicitly requires state-of-the-art elicitation (Appendix 3.2) and is voluntary. 'Almost no statute requires it', where the work happens, and the counterfactual are analytic.

faq:what-does-the-eu-ai-act-require-for-.note: 10^25 presumption (Art. 51(2)); Art. 55(1)(a)-(d) list matches; Annex XI Section 2 covers evaluation strategies and adversarial testing; reliance on codes until harmonised standards (Art. 55(2)).

faq:what-does-the-eu-ai-office-do.note: Verified: established by Commission Decision of 24 Jan 2024 within DG CNECT; enforces GPAI rules (Art. 88(1)); model access (Art. 92(3)), recall (Art. 93(1)(c)), €15M/3% fines (Art. 101); Art. 101 applies from 2 Aug 2026 (Art. 113(b)). 'Runs the Scientific Panel' is loose (the Office provides its secretariat/administrative support; the Panel advises the Office). 'A centralised role unique within EU regulatory architecture' is comparative.

entry:uk-aisi:context.note: All facts confirmed except the rename's focus list: the 14 Feb 2025 release names chem/bio weapons, cyber attacks and crime, not autonomy. 'Aligned framing with US CAISI' is analytic (and CAISI postdates the rename).

entry:caisi:desc.note: June 2025 re-establishment as CAISI by the Commerce Secretary (nist-caisi-news p1); within NIST and now titled CAISSI (caissi p1); EO 14434 of 29 Sep 2026 substitutes 'Super Intelligence' for 'AI' in executive-branch usage (eo14434 p1–p2); 2026 pre-deployment testing capacity shown by the 5 May 2026 agreements for pre-deployment evaluations (nist-bulletin p1–p2) and CAISSI's voluntary-agreement mandate (caissi p2). 'Drop safety framing' consistent with the CAISSI mission text.

entry:uk-ofcom:context.note: Illegal-content duties apply to all regulated user-to-user services with extra duties for Category 1 (osa-s7 p1–p2); codes in force Mar 2025 and recommend proactive CSAM technology (ofcom-em p1, p3; ofcom-codes p1) with no AI-specific provision (ofcom-codes p2); CPA 2026 s.248 inserts s.216A letting the Secretary of State extend duties and Ofcom's enforcement powers to AI services by regulations (cpa-s248 p1–p3), aimed at AI chatbots (pm-nofreepass p1). The closing sentence on how labs ship generators is a characterisation, not checked.

entry:uk-ofcom:cov:mit.note: Confirmed: code measures are recommended, not mandatory, and following them counts as compliance (ofcom-em p2); CSAM hash matching (ofcom-codes p1); no AI-specific measures (ofcom-codes p2); the NCII hash-matching amendment was laid before Parliament on 1 Jun 2026 (em-no2 p1; ofcom-em p4). Not confirmed from a primary text: that the NCII measure is now in force ('was added') and that the children's codes recommend age assurance.
entry:uk-ofcom:cov:mit.missing: Ofcom's statement or the issued codes showing the NCII hash-matching amendment in force (secondary reports say 30 Sep 2026) and the Protection of Children Codes' age-assurance measures; ofcom.org.uk refuses automated clients.

entry:uk-ico:desc.note: Statutory facts confirmed: office of Information Commissioner abolished and functions transferred to the Information Commission on 30 Sep 2026 (duaa-s118 p1–p2; duaa-s119 p1; si2026-1015 p1); higher maximum penalty £17.5M or 4% of worldwide turnover (dpa-s157 p1). 'Still branded ICO' and the current status of its AI guidance need ico.org.uk.
entry:uk-ico:desc.missing: ico.org.uk (AI guidance 'About this guidance' page and homepage branding) refuses automated clients; a manual check is needed.

entry:uk-ico:context.note: SI 2026/425 (in force 12 May 2026) requires the regulator to prepare a statutory code of practice on AI and automated decision-making; 'under review' understates this. Guidance dates and the Clearview/Snap investigations not re-checked (ico.org.uk blocked).

entry:uk-ico:cov:mit.note: SI 2026/425 (in force 12 May 2026) requires the regulator to prepare a statutory code of practice on AI and automated decision-making; 'under review' understates this. Guidance dates and the Clearview/Snap investigations not re-checked (ico.org.uk blocked).

entry:us-ftc:context.note: Confirmed from the Federal Register: Rytr order set aside 22 Dec 2025 as part of addressing 'unnecessary burdens' (ftc-ps p3); EO 14365 §7 directs the policy statement (eo14365 p1); the 7 Jul 2026 proposed policy statement says conflicting state laws requiring deception are impliedly preempted (ftc-ps p1–p2). Operation AI Comply (Sept 2024, five cases) and the Rite Aid five-year facial-recognition ban are not in these sources.
entry:us-ftc:context.missing: FTC press releases for Operation AI Comply (Sept 2024) and the Rite Aid stipulated order (E.D. Pa. 2:23-cv-5023); ftc.gov refuses automated clients.

edge:us-ftc|us-preempt.note: EO 14365 §7 directs the FTC Chairman to issue a policy statement on when state laws requiring altered truthful outputs are preempted (eo14365 p1); the FTC proposed it on 7 Jul 2026 (ftc-ps p1–p2). FR API shows no final version since (only an impersonation-rule proposal of 1 Oct 2026 matched 'artificial intelligence').

entry:au-esafety:context.note: Facts confirmed: standards made by the Commissioner under s.145 (au-osa p6) and codes registered under the Act; 2024 DIS standard imposes CSAM and pro-terror detection duties on high-impact generative AI services (au-dis p1–p3); 30,000 penalty units for breaching a standard or a code direction, 500 for notice breaches (au-osa p1–p2, p5); removal notices and Federal Court cessation orders (p3–p4). Note: codes are industry-developed and registered rather than 'issued' by eSafety (cf. P-0174). 'The leading non-EU model' and its influence on Five Eyes templates are comparative.
entry:au-esafety:context.missing: comparative/analytic claim; not verifiable from sources

entry:au-esafety:cov:acct.note: 30,000 penalty units for breaching an industry standard (s.146(1)) or a code direction (s.143(2)); 500 for notice breaches; removal notices (s.65 ff.); Federal Court orders to cease providing services (ss.156–159) — au-osa p1–p5.

entry:co-doi:context.note: 'Conduct bias testing' and 'document model assumptions' depend on quantitative testing rules the Division has not adopted; dates (Nov 2023; Oct 2025 extension to auto and health benefit plan insurers) confirmed. Proposal linked to P-0175. NAIC Bulletin and 'predates' claims not verifiable (content.naic.org blocked; comparative).

entry:imda:context.note: Confirmed: Model AI Governance Framework (2019; GenAI version 30 May 2024), AI Verify and the AI Verify Foundation (imda-ai p3–p6; aivf-mgfgenai p1); Veritas now a plugin in AI Verify. Not confirmed: 'adopted by major labs' and 'adapted as a regional template' (imda-ai p7 observation); MAS Guidelines on AI Risk Management (Oct 2026, effective Oct 2027) could not be re-checked because mas.gov.sg served a maintenance page.
entry:imda:context.missing: Evidence that frontier labs use AI Verify and that ASEAN states adapted it; MAS media release on the AI Risk Management Guidelines (mas.gov.sg under maintenance on 9 Nov).

entry:imda:cov:acct.note: AI Verify Foundation as a multistakeholder not-for-profit confirmed (imda-ai p4). MAS's Guidelines and their Oct 2027 effective date need mas.gov.sg, which returned a maintenance page on every attempt.
entry:imda:cov:acct.missing: MAS media release 'MAS Sets Out Supervisory Expectations on Responsible AI Adoption by Financial Institutions' (mas.gov.sg unavailable 9 Nov 2026).

entry:imda:cov:update.note: GenAI framework finalised 30 May 2024 (aivf-mgfgenai p1); agentic framework first published Jan 2026 with a May 2026 update (imda-ai p1–p2); AIVT 'continues to evolve' (p6).
